app: the care home conformance app: one app whose screens a care home's staff would use, its component bench and refusal routes as the test infrastructure they are, run under a closed set of host variants; every browser test of the framework runs on one of its screens

areas.care: a screen a care home's staff uses; it holds only what a user does
areas.bench: the component bench: the object-surface variations of the custom components, which are no business behavior
areas.refusals: one route per refusal where the view renders, each a deliberately broken view whose error the test reads
areas.delivery: a fresh app's page: an app of its own that README.md's steps alone wire on the packed packages, outside the conformance app, with no World area

harness.seed: writes the test's own data under its world key, through the world contract's typed builders: its records, the answers its endpoints script, the sampler's decision for a request, and on the twin a notice file under the world's own folder of Content, which teardown removes
harness.gate: holds a named TLA+ action of the test's world until the test releases it; the test waits until the harness reports it held, and releases the held gate that wait returns, so a release before the gate is reached does not compile; a hold takes the first request that reaches its action, or, where a test holds one action at two endpoints, the first that reaches it at the endpoint the hold names
harness.push: makes the server push a stream or hub message to the test's world and reports how many connections it reached; the harness also reports the world's open connections of a stream or hub, which a test waits on before it pushes
harness.drop: ends the test's stream or hub connection and holds the browser's next one until reopen, reporting it held
harness.refuse: answers each of the test's stream or hub connections 503 until reopen, ending an open one first, and reports each connection it refuses; a stream gives up at its next connection and a hub's start or reconnection fails
harness.reopen: lets the held next connection in, or ends a refusal
harness.restart: the test app's host script, in the layout of every screen, destroys a component's object and puts a new one on the same element when the harness tells it through the world's own channel, as the component's host does, and reports it done; no page holds a control for it
harness.clock: Playwright's Page.Clock, for every page timer: a plan's waits and the hub client's start and reconnection waits; a stream's reconnection runs on the browser's own timer, outside the clock, after the retry: the harness's stream endpoints write
harness.gc: Playwright's Page.RequestGCAsync, confirmed by the page's own weak hold

partKinds.native: a plain element or a hand-written control in the view's markup: the core reaches an element by id (M5.N1) and markup raises an app event from it (M1.D3); never a framework input, which a consumer renders (M7.N2)

harnessTests.page: The world's records page, a page of the app's World area that lists the residents of the request's world as text the server writes, no framework part on it.
harnessTests.gesture: Seed the resident Ada in a first world and Ben in a second, each browser context with its own world cookie, and open the records page in each.
harnessTests.outcome: The first world's page lists Ada and not Ben; the second world's lists Ben and not Ada.
harnessTests.opposite: With Ada and Ben both seeded in the first world, its records page lists Ada and Ben.
harnessTests.defect: The world middleware scopes no seeded data to the world's key, so each records page lists both residents.

harnessTests.page: The world's word page, a page of the app's World area with no framework part on it: a link that opens, in the page's frame, the world's word endpoint, which answers with the word the world's seed holds as text the server writes.
harnessTests.gesture: Seed the word North, arm the gate on the word endpoint's answer, click the link, wait until the harness reports the gate held, seed the word South, then release the gate the wait returned held.
harnessTests.outcome: The frame shows South: the gate parked the request before its endpoint ran, so the answer was computed at the release, from the word the world held then.
harnessTests.opposite: With no gate armed, seeding North and clicking the link shows North in the frame.
harnessTests.defect: The gate does not hold the endpoint's answer until its release, so the endpoint reads North before the test seeds South and the frame shows North; or the harness never reports the gate held, so the wait fails.

harnessTests.page: The world's records page, opened in a browser context that carries no world cookie, beside the same page in a world a test seeded.
harnessTests.gesture: Seed the resident Ada in a world, then open the records page in a context with no world cookie and in the seeded world's context.
harnessTests.outcome: The person's page shows its heading Residents and lists no resident: the document request that carried no world was given a world of its own.
harnessTests.opposite: The seeded world's page lists Ada.
harnessTests.defect: The world middleware opens no world for a document request that carries none, so the person's page fails and shows no heading; or it puts that request in a world another context holds, so the person's page lists Ada.

harnessTests.page: The world's words page, a page of the app's World area with no framework part on it: two links, each opening in a frame of its own one of the world's two word endpoints, which each answer with the word the world's seed holds as text the server writes.
harnessTests.gesture: Seed the word North, arm the gate on each word endpoint's answer, naming the endpoint, click both links, wait until the harness reports each gate held, seed the word South and release the second endpoint's gate, then seed the word East and release the first's.
harnessTests.outcome: After the second release its frame shows South while the first frame shows no answer, and after the first release its frame shows East: each hold parked its own endpoint's request until its own release.
harnessTests.opposite: With the gate armed on the first endpoint alone, seeding North and clicking the second link shows North in the second frame.
harnessTests.defect: A hold that names an endpoint parks the first request that reaches its gate at any endpoint, so the second link's request waits on the first endpoint's hold and the second frame stays empty; or a second arm of one gate replaces the first, so the first hold is never reported held.

harnessTests.page: The world's word desk, a page of the app's World area with no framework part on it: a link that opens, in the page's frame, an action of an MVC controller of the app, whose filter reaches the answer gate with the action's own address and which answers with the word the world's seed holds as text the server writes.
harnessTests.gesture: Seed the word North, arm the gate on the action's answer, naming its endpoint, click Ask the desk, wait until the harness reports the gate held, seed the word South, then release the gate the wait returned held.
harnessTests.outcome: The frame shows South: the action's filter parked the request before the action ran, so the answer was computed at the release, from the word the world held then.
harnessTests.opposite: With no gate armed, seeding North and clicking Ask the desk shows North in the frame.
harnessTests.defect: The action's filter does not reach the answer gate, or reaches it with another address than the action's, so the action reads North before the test seeds South and the frame shows North, or the harness never reports the gate held and the wait fails.

harnessTests.page: The world's word slip, a page of the app's World area with no framework part on it: an action of an MVC controller of the app writes the word the world's seed holds and the count of its letters as the app's JSON options write them, as text the server writes.
harnessTests.gesture: Open a world under numbersAsText, a host the fixture does not run under, seed the word East and open the word slip.
harnessTests.outcome: The slip reads {"word":"East","letters":"4"}: the world's seed and its page reached the server of the host the test named, whose options write a number as text.
harnessTests.opposite: A world of the fixture's own host, net10, seeded North, reads {"word":"North","letters":5}.
harnessTests.defect: The world opens under the fixture's own host, or the app sets net10's options whatever host it starts under, so the slip reads {"word":"East","letters":4}; or the seed goes to the fixture's host while the page opens under the named one, so the slip reads {"word":"","letters":"0"}.

harnessTests.page: The world's zone slip, a page of the app's World area with no framework part on it: a paragraph its own script fills with the hour and minute the browser's clock reads for the instant 2026-01-15T12:00:00Z.
harnessTests.gesture: Open a world whose browser runs in Asia/Kolkata, a zone the fixture does not name, and open the zone slip.
harnessTests.outcome: The slip reads 17:30: the world's browser runs in the zone the test named.
harnessTests.opposite: A world of the fixture's own, whose browser runs in America/Los_Angeles, reads 04:00.
harnessTests.defect: The world opens its browser in America/Los_Angeles whatever zone the test names, so the Kolkata world's slip reads 04:00; or in the host's zone, America/New_York, so it reads 07:00.

harnessTests.page: The world's culture slip, a page of the app's World area with no framework part on it: an action of an MVC controller of the app writes the name of the sort its request's culture compares text by and the number 1234.5 as that culture writes it with one decimal, as text the server writes.
harnessTests.gesture: Open the culture slip at its address under the German phonebook sort, culture=de-DE_phoneb.
harnessTests.outcome: The slip reads de-DE_phoneb 1.234,5: the request bound and rendered under the culture its address named, the phonebook sort kept.
harnessTests.opposite: The culture slip opened at its address with no culture reads en-US 1,234.5, whatever culture the machine runs under.
harnessTests.defect: The app ignores the query, so the slip reads en-US 1,234.5 under the phonebook's address; or it resolves the culture by its name, which drops the alternate sort, so the slip reads de-DE 1.234,5; or a request with no culture reads the machine's.

harnessTests.page: The world's culture slip, at its address under fr-FR, a culture the app does not serve.
harnessTests.gesture: Open the culture slip at its address under culture=fr-FR.
harnessTests.outcome: The page reads The culture query names one of en-US, de-DE, tr-TR, haw-US, de-DE_phoneb and invariant, once.
harnessTests.opposite: The culture slip opened under culture=de-DE reads de-DE 1.234,5.
harnessTests.defect: An unserved culture is served as en-US or as the machine's, so the page shows a slip, en-US 1,234.5, and a test that names a culture by mistake runs under another.

harnessTests.page: The world's host page, a page of the app's World area with no plan on it: a ConformanceCallbacks at the id callbacks whose own function names its generation, which the conformance library's script builds on alis:mount.
harnessTests.gesture: Click Raise room 7, restart the object at callbacks through the harness, then click Raise room 7.
harnessTests.outcome: Before the restart the log's one line reads own 1, and after it the log's one line reads own 2: when the restart returned, the host script had destroyed the first object, emptied its element and built the second there.
harnessTests.opposite: In a world with no restart, the second Raise room 7 writes a second line, and the log reads own 1 twice.
harnessTests.defect: The restart returns before the page's script has done it, or the script builds no new object, so the second click reaches the first object and the log reads own 1 twice; or the script leaves the first object's controls beside the second's, so two buttons are named Raise room 7 and the click is refused.
